races.name: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Fillies Maiden
Matchbook Exchange Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Tally-Ho Stud Irish EBF Ballyogan Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Chantez
runners_data.note: A 4yo gelding by Churchill whose recent form (38-544) is modest but whose prominent style suits strong gallops — the key issue is that with Dancing Saxon, Soul Love, and Havana Anna all eyeing prominent positions, Gary Carroll may find himself shuffled back further than ideal, blunting his chance in a shape that needs him closer.|
runners_data.comment: Chantez showed clear promise with a third five starts back and arrives fresh after 32 days off, holding experience over today's trip and going, with our rating of 96 marking her as a genuine danger; the risk is she remains yet to win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: First Instinct
runners_data.note: William Haggas's hold-up filly brings her two best runs at 6f on Good (2nd and 1st), making this trip and ground combination her optimal conditions; Cieren Fallon provides a strong tactical presence and her OR of 105 gives her genuine class claims if she gets a clean run from off the pace.|
runners_data.comment: First Instinct catches the eye with a second last time out and a win five starts back, and she has experience of both today's trip and going; at 133 lb from stall 4, the weight she shoulders is the key question mark.

runners_data.name: Temperance
runners_data.note: Racing off just 9 days means fitness is not in doubt, and the blinkers (hg:p) sharpen her focus; a genuine hold-up type who handles Good ground well (12/14 sim-going runs), but her OR of 84 makes it a tall order against several higher-rated rivals — needs pace to collapse rather than merely be honest.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Temperance has run over today's trip and going before, but her recent form has been largely mid-to-rear, and carrying 133 lb from stall two leaves her with plenty to prove despite a speed rating of 87.

runners_data.name: Treasure Rose
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's filly has a sharp winning profile on Good ground (1/6f/GOO, 1/7f/SOF) and Ben Coen gives her tactical options, but she is a natural front-tracker who is likely to find Dancing Saxon and Soul Love ahead of her in the queue — her chance hinges on her adaptability if held up further back than ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures and with an 8th last time out preceding a 5th the run before, Treasure Rose faces an uphill task, though she has run over today's trip and going, returns fit on a nine-day turnaround, and does boast two wins in her last six starts.

runners_data.name: Dancing Saxon
runners_data.note: A lightly raced 3yo for Joseph O'Brien who arrives on a hot run of form (two wins from last three, 6f and 7f GOO) and looks the most likely horse to press Havana Anna from early on; McDonogh is a strong tactical rider and an OR of 96, still on the upgrade, makes him one of the most interesting prominently-raced horses in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Dancing Saxon arrives on the back of three wins in her last five starts, including a victory last time out, and has experience of today's distance and going; however, her 130 lb burden is a stiff ask, and our rating of 94 suggests she faces stronger rivals here.

runners_data.name: Focaccia
runners_data.note: A 3yo filly from J A Stack who has struggled at higher levels in recent starts (717828) but does have a win at 5f on Good; she naturally wants to be prominent but with a clutch of higher-class rivals claiming that ground, she may end up racing in an unfamiliar rearward position — her OR of 78 represents a meaningful class concession.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of eight on our figures, Focaccia has been inconsistent in recent starts, with an eighth last time out and only one win in her last six; a second two starts back offers slim encouragement, and she has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Havana Anna
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's confirmed front-runner carries an OR of 108, the highest in the field, and arrives on a career-best effort (1/6f/GOO); Gavin Ryan knows her pattern well and Good ground suits her three wins perfectly — the pace dynamic is built around her and her ability to control tempo is the axis of this race.|
runners_data.comment: Havana Anna shaped well when a winner three starts back, and she has experience of today's trip and going to call upon; the concern is that she has not recaptured that form in her last two outings, finishing seventh most recently.

runners_data.name: Soul Love
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's 3yo filly has a superb record on Good ground at 6f (three wins at 1/6f/GOO, including a G3 recently) and Jamin can be a potent finisher from a prominent position; an OR of 101 gives her genuine claims, and she is one of the horses most likely to secure a clean pitch just behind Havana Anna without being redistributed.|
runners_data.comment: Soul Love arrives here with three wins in her last five starts, including a victory last time out, and she handles today's distance and going having tackled both before; carrying 130 lb from stall seven, she makes appeal on that profile.

races.paceDynamic: Havana Anna is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead at a comparable rating, she is likely to dictate a controlled, honest gallop from the off on Good ground at Naas. Soul Love and Dancing Saxon are the truest prominent types likely to slot in directly behind her, with Dancing Saxon's recent winning form suggesting he will press up early and keep the pace honest without turning it into a sprint. This is a race where the pace will be real but not frantic — enough to test the field over 6f on a flat track, but managed rather than ruthless, which broadly favours hold-up horses with a turn of foot to land a late blow. The field contains more prominent/front-running types than the pace map can accommodate: Chantez, Treasure Rose, and Focaccia are all natural prominent racers but at least two of them will be unable to secure their preferred position, with Dancing Saxon and Soul Love holding the stronger claims to the berths just off Havana Anna.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Havana Anna Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Havana Anna secures an uncontested lead and the redistributed prominent types fail to pressure her through the race.
scenarios.body: Havana Anna dictates a sustainable tempo and, with no rival willing or able to take her on, conserves enough energy to quicken clear in the final furlong; on Good ground at Naas and with Gavin Ryan a key ally, her superior OR of 108 gives her the class edge over most of the field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to stretch the field and the closers get a clear run through from off the pace.
scenarios.body: First Instinct and Temperance are both genuine hold-up horses who have the finishing speed to pick off tiring rivals if the front end has been run off its feet; First Instinct's Good-ground form is strong (2/6f/GOO) and Cieren Fallon is well capable of timing a late challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent midfield types secures a better position than expected and strikes before the leaders tire.
scenarios.body: Dancing Saxon is the likeliest beneficiary here, with two recent wins at 6f and an OR of 96 that suggests he is still on the upgrade; if he tracks Havana Anna closely and quickens half a furlong out, his course-distance form gives him a live chance in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Finish, Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the field bunches and the outcome is decided by a late, chaotic sprint inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A messy race where redistributed types racing out of their natural roles — Chantez, Treasure Rose, Focaccia — cause interference or position-scrambling; in this low-probability shape, any horse with tactical versatility and a clear passage could benefit, but it is the least likely outcome given Havana Anna's established front-running pattern.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Chantez, Treasure Rose, or Focaccia break sharply and attempt to bypass Soul Love and Dancing Saxon for the prominent positions — a scramble for spots in the first furlong could disrupt pace plans and compromise Havana Anna's clean lead.

Monitor First Instinct's position at the 2f mark — if she is boxed in behind a wall of prominent types with nowhere to go, her finishing kick (which requires a clear run) will be wasted regardless of conditions being ideal.

Dancing Saxon's racing weight of 130lbs as a 3yo carrying a penalty is worth noting — if he has to work hard early to maintain his position against older, heavier rivals, his stamina reserves for the final furlong could be tested.

Temperance's quick 9-day turnaround with headgear applied and a modest trainer strike rate (0/3 in 14 days) means there is a fitness and confidence question — watch her in the paddock and early stalls behaviour before drawing strong conclusions.

Going confirmed Good all day at Naas across multiple distances — no meaningful bias to exploit, but note that all the strongest recent form in this field was achieved on Good or Good-to-Soft, meaning no runner faces a hidden ground concern.

races.name: Big Evs At Tally-Ho Handicap

runners_data.name: Aurora Nova
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old hold-up type who has placed three times in similar Good-ground sprints recently; Sam Coen (5) takes the ride for a trainer who has had one winner from four in the past 14 days, and the step back to 5f (where she finished third on soft last time) gives mild encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Aurora Nova nonetheless catches the eye with a third five starts back and a speed rating well clear of her official rating, suggesting she retains ability; the weight of 142 lb from stall 13 is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Dandy Land
runners_data.note: The key pace-setter in this race and the only confirmed front-runner; recent form at 5f on Good is solid with a win and two places in her last three, and while she carries headgear (visor) her style fit is flagged slightly out of role at 0.93, meaning she may be more prominent than pure leader — the McCreery yard has one winner from 15 runners over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Menwirr
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old hold-up type returning from 89 days off with just one run in comparable going across four starts; Denis Hogan's operation has been busy (2/19 T14) but this colt's form on Good ground is thin, and stepping down from 7f to 5f over Naas is unproven.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and not seen out for 89 days, Menwirr faces a stiff task from stall nine carrying 140 lb, though he has run over today's trip before and that experience offers some small encouragement.

runners_data.name: Nebrook Star
runners_data.note: Held up from a wide gate by Jamie Orr (7) for Diego Dias, who has one winner from five in the past fortnight; Best 5f form came on Good (third and fourth) but recent form on Stalls tracks doesn't translate directly, and the hood (b) is worn again.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Nebrook Star at least has experience of today's trip and going to call upon, but recent form has trended the wrong way and she faces a stiff task from stall one carrying 140 lb.

runners_data.name: Tawaazon
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old hold-up specialist with outstanding course and distance credentials — 13 runs on Good producing one win and three places — making him the most experienced in this sphere; Chris Hayes rides for a trainer without a runner in the last 14 days, but the horse's profile suits a scenario where something goes wrong up front.
runners_data.comment: Tawaazon has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 67 — ten pounds clear of his official mark — flags him as a leading danger, with a second in recent starts suggesting he can threaten at his best; the risk is that he has been winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Gordon Bennett
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old hold-up type who has been struggling for form, finishing no better than sixth in his last five outings, all at 6f or beyond; Ben Coen takes the ride but the drop to 5f and patchy Good-ground record (9/15) offer limited confidence.
runners_data.comment: Ranked top of 19 by our rating, Gordon Bennett brings strong form credentials to this field, finishing third three starts back and unplaced 17 days ago with distance and going experience to call on; the risk is he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: I'm Spartacus
runners_data.note: One of the more consistent prominent-style horses in the field; Adam Caffrey's mount has won over 6f on Good and placed at the same course, and with McGuinness's yard in terrific form (4/23 T14) this prominent racer is well positioned to track Dandy Land and fire in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Fresh from a 30-day break and with experience of today's trip and conditions, I'm Spartacus shaped with promise when fourth two starts back, and he showed what he can do when taking top honours five starts back; carrying 137 lb from stall 14 on a rating of 55, our figures suggest he merits plenty of respect here.

runners_data.name: Pansy Poe
runners_data.note: Returns from 331 days off for Mark Fahey, who has no runner in the T14 window, with a tongue-tie applied; hold-up style and limited 5f form on Good make this a fitness-question runner whose chance hinges on the layoff not blunting her sharpness.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and returning after 331 days off, Pansy Poe faces a stiff ask, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a rating of 58 gives her a slim foothold in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Simmering Seas
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old whose best effort was a 5f Good win but who is flagged as a fader in finishes; Terry Casey (7) rides for a yard with one winner from seven over 14 days, and though mapped to midfield this horse is a true hold-up runner who would naturally track further back — the style mismatch (0.90 fit) is a meaningful discount.
runners_data.comment: Simmering Seas shaped well when second last time out, but she remains winless in her last five starts and that sixth three starts back underlines her inconsistency; experience over today's trip and going gives her a foothold, though stall 12 and 134 lb are factors to weigh.

runners_data.name: Smart Sioux
runners_data.note: Genuinely races from behind and has struggled in similar Good-ground fields, with no wins or places in nine starts on Good; Robbie Colgan takes the mount but the fade-in-finish flag combined with being mapped forward of natural position (0.91 fit) means this is among the harder cases to back with confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Smart Sioux faces a stiff task from stall 10 carrying 134 lb, though she has run over today's distance and going before and our rating of 62 suggests she holds more ability than her official mark implies.

runners_data.name: Hasiyna
runners_data.note: A 6-year-old hold-up type returning from 156 days off; all Hasiyna's best form has come on Soft/Standard at the Curragh rather than Good, and Siobhan Rutledge inherits the ride for a very busy McConnell yard (4/27 T14) — the going and layoff both need to be overcome before this style mismatch becomes relevant.
runners_data.comment: Hasiyna showed a second and a win in her recent starts, but a seventh last time out and 156 days off the track are clear concerns; she has run over today's trip and going before and carries 132 lb from stall two.

runners_data.name: Whatswrongnow
runners_data.note: A prominent-style runner who has placed four times in 15 Good-ground starts without winning; Adam Browne-Souza (7) is the jockey for a trainer without a recent runner, and the horse's consistency just off the pace makes it a legitimate each-way profile if Dandy Land's lead is pegged back late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 15 of 19 on our figures, Whatswrongnow faces a stiff ask from stall 19 carrying 132 lb, though experience over today's trip and going and a return to form shown by a third three starts back offer slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Prada's World
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old returning from a staggering 484-day absence; Luke McAteer takes the ride but the horse's hold-up profile and best form at 7-8f rather than 5f, combined with the extended layoff, make this a speculative inclusion regardless of style redistribution.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and absent for 484 days, Prada's World faces a stiff ask on her return, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a third two starts back offers a crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Amanirenas
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old genuine hold-up horse whose lone win in this sample came on Standard ground over 6f; mapped to midfield because of field congestion at the rear, the horse is a true closer whose fade-in-finish flag and 331-day absence are compounding negatives despite a decent Good-ground record overall.
runners_data.comment: Amanirenas won two starts back but has been out of the frame since, and 331 days off the track is a significant query on fitness; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 130 lb is no light burden, though a rating of 62 gives her something to work with.

runners_data.name: Step Back In Time
runners_data.note: A prominent-style 8-year-old who has actually won 5f on Good twice in recent form — the most strike-rate-rich of the prominent types at this course and trip; Rory Cleary rides for Chris Timmons, and the horse's 13/15 Good-ground starts make him a respected threat to hold his place just off the leader.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked well down the field on our figures, Step Back In Time faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and comes into this a shade fresher after 20 days off.

runners_data.name: Steel Magnolia
runners_data.note: W J Lee takes the ride on this 4-year-old for the McCreery stable, which has the in-form runner Dandy Land in the same heat; prominent style with multiple placed efforts over 5f on Good and soft gives Steel Magnolia legitimate claims to be the best of the chasers given the going record (7/15 Good).
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 14th of 19 on our figures, Steel Magnolia faces a stiff task from stall 18 carrying 127 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and her second last time out shows she retains some ability.

runners_data.name: Little Roy
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced 3-year-old with only three career starts, all of which resulted in defeats; Leigh Roche rides for Gillian Scott (1 winner from 3 T14), and while the fade-in-finish flag and mapping away from natural hold-up position are contextual points, inexperience over 5f Good is the core concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked 18 of 19 on our figures, Little Roy faces a stiff ask here; 70 days off the track does little to inspire confidence, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Niobite
runners_data.note: Has run four times and finished no better than twelfth, all on Good ground; Robyn Donaghue-Leahy (7) partners for Patrick Flynn (1/5 T14), and the tongue-tie worn again does little to offset a form profile that reads uniformly poorly — fade-in-finish flag and position mismatch add further caution.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Niobite faces a stiff task from stall 17, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a manageable 30-day break.

runners_data.name: Lismacbryan
runners_data.note: A 5-year-old hold-up type returning from 87 days off; best form has come on Good over 6f rather than 5f, and hood (h) is worn — Zoe McMullan (10) takes the ride for a trainer with no runners in the last 14 days, and this is another true rear-tracker mapped to midfield because of the field's hold-up surplus.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 17 of 19 on our figures, Lismacbryan makes the most of an 87-day absence hard to assess, though she has run over today's trip and going before and carries a manageable 122 lb from stall seven.

races.paceDynamic: Dandy Land is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 19-runner 5f handicap, and with no other genuine pace-setters to push her, she is set to control proceedings from the gates at a comfortable, sustainable gallop on Good ground at Naas. I'm Spartacus, Whatswrongnow, Step Back In Time, and Steel Magnolia will press from prominent positions just behind, providing a light degree of pressure but unlikely to seriously disrupt Dandy Land's rhythm. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Smart Sioux, Simmering Seas, Hasiyna, Lismacbryan, and Prada's World are all true come-from-behind horses but have been mapped to midfield given the congestion; of those, Smart Sioux and Simmering Seas are most likely to actually claim a midfield berth rather than their natural rearward pitch. With one horse dictating an uncontested lead over the minimum trip on a fair surface, this race shape heavily favours horses capable of tracking close to the pace and quickening from a prominent position — true hold-up horses racing from further back than ideal will face a stern ask to close in five furlongs when no searching early tempo is guaranteed to stretch the field for them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dandy Land Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Dandy Land breaks cleanly and faces no early pressure, setting a controlled pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Dandy Land dictates entirely on her own terms, ensuring a steady-to-moderate gallop that plays to the stamina of those tracking her; the prominent runners immediately behind her are best placed to exploit any late weakness.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Movers Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves just quick enough to string the field out and the prominent trio land a telling blow in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: I'm Spartacus and Whatswrongnow, both sitting a length or two off the pace, get a clear run into the final furlong and use their good-ground form to overhaul the leader; Steel Magnolia's strong recent 5f form at this trip makes her a natural beneficiary of this shape too.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is just quick enough to see the leaders tire and the midfield horses cover ground efficiently to the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Tawaazon and Aurora Nova, both genuine midfield operators with multiple placed efforts in similar going, get a run between horses and pounce; this scenario requires a faster-than-expected gallop set by Dandy Land which is not her natural mode.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Hold-Up Horses Swooping
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and the horses camping at the rear find daylight for a late charge.
scenarios.body: This outcome requires horses like Smart Sioux and Simmering Seas — redistributed from their natural rear position and flagged as fading finishers — to produce uncharacteristic finishing bursts, making this the least likely shape given their style misfit and form record.

watchPoints.text: Dandy Land's break from the stalls is critical — if she misses the kick or is crowded on the rail, the one-horse pace advantage evaporates and the entire race shape collapses, opening the door for the prominent quartet to race ungoverned.
I'm Spartacus and Step Back In Time are both prominent types drawn in a 19-runner field; watch for crowding on the turn that could block their run into the straight at the crucial moment.

Steel Magnolia and Dandy Land are both trained by W McCreery — with two runners in the same race, the yard's tactics may involve one horse being ridden to set things up for the other, which could alter how aggressively Steel Magnolia is asked to go early.

Several horses mapped to midfield — including Smart Sioux, Simmering Seas, and Hasiyna — are true hold-up types unable to get their natural position; if the early pace is slow, these runners will be caught wide or stuck in traffic with insufficient sprint to close over five furlongs.

Pansy Poe and Amanirenas both return from layoffs exceeding 300 days — monitor market moves on either in the final hour before the race, as any significant support would suggest strong home confidence in their fitness despite the long absence.

races.name: Hartes Group Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Eastern Peace
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer for Ross O'Sullivan who has shown ability over shorter Good-ground trips (6th/9f/GOO recently); drops back in to a big field after 31 days off and needs to improve on a form string reading 19-305, but the stable also saddles Tero d'Rosa so watch for any stable lean.|
runners_data.comment: Eastern Peace shaped with clear promise when third three starts back, and she has run over today's trip and going, suggesting conditions pose no concern; the main worry is that she has been out of the frame in her last two runs.

runners_data.name: Glittering Gem
runners_data.note: D K Weld's confirmed pace-setter, last ran just 8 days ago (4th/12f/GOO) and has a solid recent record on Good going (3 from 5 in similar conditions); races slightly out of role here as a P-type asked to lead, but with no rivals to press her she can dictate on her own terms.|
runners_data.comment: Glittering Gem has shown consistency in recent starts, finishing second and third in her last three runs, though she remains yet to score and carries 140 lb from stall 12; experience over today's trip and going gives her a fair platform.

runners_data.name: Showyoutheropes
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator for the O'Leary yard fitted with a visor; Good ground suits (1 win and 4 places from 9 similar-going runs) and the 12f-13f trip is his optimum, but a field of 18 with mostly rear-dwellers means he will need a clear passage in the straight.|
runners_data.comment: Showyoutheropes brings solid course-experience credentials, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 71 edges his official mark, making him a lively fourth-ranked threat in an 18-runner field; the concern is he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Sinbad My Dad
runners_data.note: Stays in the rear for Seamus Fahey and has form on Good ground over 10f (4th) though he has drifted back in the field in recent outings; the 5/7 apprentice claim for Harnett could be useful in this competitive handicap but his form string of 98649 demands he improves sharply.|
runners_data.comment: Sinbad My Dad has run over today's trip and going, and a 17-day turnaround keeps him fresh, while his rating of 71 marks him as a genuine threat in this field; yet to score in his last five starts, the consistency of those finishes is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Derry Lad
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran running in a tongue-strap and cheekpieces for Kevin Thomas Coleman; has been remarkably consistent in finishing 5th repeatedly over 11-15f on Good ground (5 of last 5 in GOO-type going) but that string also shows a ceiling — he places but rarely wins.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Derry Lad has nonetheless shown consistency with four successive fifth-place finishes, and he has experience of today's trip and going; carrying 134 lb from stall nine, he looks capable of running into the frame without threatening at the sharp end.

runners_data.name: Covert Legend
runners_data.note: Tough hold-up type from Maurice Ahern; his natural position is at the rear but with this field saturated by closers he is unlikely to get the backmarker berth he prefers — the STYLE_FIT of 0.91 flags that his chance is mildly compromised if forced to race closer than ideal. Wears a tongue-strap and has placed twice from six Good-ground runs.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Covert Legend does offer three fourths and a second in recent form, though that eighth last time out is a concern; has run over today's trip and going, and 20 days between runs suggests he arrives reasonably fresh, yet his rating of 63 leaves him mid-pack in this field.

runners_data.name: Maralinga
runners_data.note: Veteran stayer who fades in finishes and has been finishing in the back half of big fields over marathon trips (10th-19th in recent runs over 16-17f); dropping to 1m3f could help but his redistribution means he is unlikely to find the natural rear-of-field position that suits, and his fade tendency is a concern.|
runners_data.comment: Maralinga won five starts back, but nothing better than fourth since then does temper any confidence; 44 days off makes fitness a question mark, though he has run over today's trip and going and carries 133 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Parish Team
runners_data.note: Bolger three-year-old who is 0-from-3 with a run of 880, all on Good ground; carries top weight relative to age (132lbs) and has faded in all recent runs — no encouraging angles here and the big field will compound his tendency to struggle.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked 16 of 18 on our figures, Parish Team faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's going before and 17 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, but consecutive eighth-place finishes make it hard to fancy him at the weights.

runners_data.name: God Knows
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old P Sweeney horse who is a true hold-up type by inclination but is placed in midfield on the map due to rear congestion; his best efforts have come on Heavier ground (2nd/8f/HEA) and with apprentice Adam Grant aboard in a field of 18, finding daylight may be the primary challenge.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, God Knows did finish second five starts back and shaped with more ability than her recent efforts suggest; she has run over today's trip and going, carries 131 lb from stall 3, and a rating of 78 marks her as the one to beat in this field.

runners_data.name: Signor Ferrari
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for P J F Murphy who maps naturally close to the pace; three places from six good-ground runs over similar trips is encouraging, and at OR 61 he has room to improve — the 7lb claim for Conor Cusack adds value if he can travel sweetly in second or third.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Signor Ferrari does at least bring experience of today's trip and going, and a third two runs back suggests he retains some ability; however, 131 lb from stall 16 makes life harder for a gelding rated just 61 officially.

runners_data.name: Tero d'Rosa
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's other runner — a genuine hold-up type by history (won over 10f/GOO, placed over 10f/STA) who is mapped to midfield because too many horses want to race at the rear; the STYLE_FIT discount of 0.92 is modest, and with 42 days since his last run freshness could be a positive if he settles.|
runners_data.comment: Tero d'Rosa showed he can win when landing a first four starts back, but three subsequent efforts have yielded a pair of sixths and a fourth, suggesting he's found a level; has run over today's trip and going, though 131 lb and stall 15 are factors to weigh.

runners_data.name: Amavasya
runners_data.note: Won over 10f/GOO most recently for M C Grassick and wears a hood; returning from 79 days off is the key query, but Good ground and a step back to 1m3f suit his profile — he is a hold-up type redistributed to midfield, meaning he will likely race closer than ideal, which could actually help him strike earlier than usual.|
runners_data.comment: Amavasya won last time out but has been inconsistent in recent starts, and a 79-day absence gives pause; she has run over today's trip and going before, though carrying 130 lb from stall 11 will test her stamina for a return.

runners_data.name: God Of Thunder
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's seven-year-old wearing a tongue-strap and cheekpieces; placed over extreme trips (2nd/18f, 7th/16f on GOO) suggesting stamina is fine but ability to win on a fair surface at this trip is unproven — ran just 8 days ago and his redistribution to midfield means he may not get the patient ride he needs.|
runners_data.comment: God Of Thunder has experience over today's trip and ground, but winless in his last six starts and drawn in stall 18, he arrives off a seventh last time out and a sixth two starts back, with his sole spark of encouragement a third five starts back.

runners_data.name: Wie Wunderbar
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old from Jessica Harrington's yard with only three runs and a style marked UNKNOWN; has placed (3rd and 2nd) but form is slim and going/style profile is genuinely uncertain — the 72-day absence adds further caution, though Harrington's T14 record of 1/29 is subdued.|
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and yet to win in her last three starts, Wie Wunderbar shaped with promise when second last time out and third three starts back, suggesting she remains open to improvement on her return from 72 days off carrying 125 lb from stall 14.

runners_data.name: Walls Cross
runners_data.note: Unplaced in all four career starts (form 0800) and fades in finishes; a hold-up type squeezed into midfield on the map and returning after just 11 days, Timothy Doyle's four-year-old has shown nothing from limited opportunities to suggest she can reverse those trends in an 18-runner handicap.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked fifteenth of eighteen on our figures, Walls Cross faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and returns on a sharp turnaround of eleven days, but the recent form makes her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Millhone
runners_data.note: Charles Weld's three-year-old who has placed twice over 11-12f on Good ground (2nd, 2nd) and wears a hood; form of 07922 shows improvement but the fade-in-finish flag and the redistribution away from his natural trailing position means he may need a stronger pace than Glittering Gem is likely to set.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Millhone has at least shown consistency at this level with a pair of runner-up finishes in her most recent outings, and she has run over today's trip and going before, but ranked 13 of 18 on our figures she faces a stiff task from stall 13 carrying 121 lb.

runners_data.name: Yquem
runners_data.note: Richard Brabazon's four-year-old with a progressive record on Good ground (won 9f/GOO, placed 9f and 10f/GOO) and ran just 5 days ago; his form string of 891344 reads like a horse finding form and the Good going is familiar — he is a hold-up type shifted forward by the map, which could suit if he travels kindly.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 18 on our figures, Yquem faces a stiff ask, with consecutive fourths in her latest two starts and only one win in her last six; she does have experience over today's trip and going, but 5 days between runs and stall 17 are the neutral facts here.

runners_data.name: Miss Ivor
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from P O'Rourke who is winless in five starts on Good ground and carries a fade-in-finish flag; best efforts have come over sprint trips (7f, 6f) making 1m3f a significant test of stamina — nothing in her profile suggests she can be competitive in this company at this distance.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Miss Ivor faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 16 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh, but that is about as far as the case for her goes.

races.paceDynamic: Glittering Gem is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rivals capable of forcing a contested gallop — she is likely to bowl along in front at a measured, sustainable tempo on Good ground over 1m3f at Naas. With the pace map saturated by hold-up types, the vast majority of runners will be tracking or chasing from midfield to rear, meaning the field will almost certainly string out behind one honest pace-setter rather than race in a compressed group. The resulting shape — a single controlled lead, minimal pressure through the middle stages, and a stamina-testing stretch run — strongly favours horses who can sit just off the pace or in close-touch midfield and sustain a long, grinding finish rather than produce a sharp late kick. Prominent racers and in-touch midfielders who travel smoothly into the straight will have the clearest passage; the redistributed hold-up horses (Covert Legend, Maralinga, Tero d'Rosa, God Knows, Amavasya, God Of Thunder, Millhone, Yquem, Miss Ivor, Walls Cross) cannot all find their natural rear-of-field position and those forced forward may not settle, while the true closers will need this controlled tempo to set up a strong late run — but with 1m3f and only one honest gallop, the window for a devastating late charge is narrow, tilting the balance firmly toward prominent-seated or close-tracking types who can strike from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Glittering Gem Controls, Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Glittering Gem leads at a fair but unchallenged tempo and holds her advantage into the straight, allowing close-tracking horses to make their move from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Glittering Gem dictates every fraction unchallenged, ensuring the race is run at an honest but not punishing gallop, and runners in close attendance entering the straight enjoy first run on the field; at 1m3f on Good ground this suits horses who travel well and stay strongly rather than those requiring a truly searching early pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Through Tiring Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to soften the leaders and hold-up horses can navigate traffic and close powerfully from the rear in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: A genuine gallop would string the field out and leave the front-runners vulnerable late; any hold-up horse who avoids being hampered in a large, compact group could pick off tired rivals with a strong sustained finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Glittering Gem Defies Field Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Glittering Gem finds the tempo she sets so comfortable that no rival can mount a sustained challenge and she simply stays on unopposed.
scenarios.body: On Good ground at 1m3f with no rival willing to press her, she conserves energy through every furlong and simply lengthens away entering the final 2f; D K Weld's yard is in form (2/18 in the T14 window) and this scenario is live if the jockey rides her with confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Large Field, Outsider Profits
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems, a false pace, or positional errors shuffle the race order dramatically, leaving an unexpected challenger to emerge late.
scenarios.body: With 18 runners and apprentice jockeys dominating the saddles, navigational errors in a compacted midfield group are a genuine risk, and a horse who happens to find a clear run from a decent position at the 2f pole could catch the market off-guard.

watchPoints.text: Watch Glittering Gem's early behaviour — if Sam Coen takes her back from her natural prominent role rather than leading, the entire race shape loses its one pace-setter and the tempo could collapse, benefiting unexpected horses.

With 18 runners and a field dominated by hold-up types, severe traffic congestion in the straight is a real risk — horses drawn wide or with patient jockeys (Showyoutheropes, Sinbad My Dad) will need a clear run and any blockage could cost them the race.

Amavasya returns from 79 days off for M C Grassick and wore a hood last time when winning — monitor her pre-race behaviour and whether the hood is fitted, as a fresh horse in a big field can be unpredictable.

Yquem ran only five days ago (LR:5d) for Richard Brabazon — watch the betting market closely as connections would not run a horse back so quickly without confidence, and his Good-ground form is quietly progressive.|

races.name: TRM BIOACTIVE Energy Boost Handicap

runners_data.name: Alice Monet
runners_data.note: D K Weld's filly boasts solid good-ground form with two wins from five similar-going starts and comes here 18 days fresh; a hold-up type who will need traffic to clear, but her OR=96 and recent Goodwood third suggest she is the classiest late-runner in this field.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a winner twice in her last five starts, Alice Monet returns on a handy 18-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and going; drawn in stall one carrying 140 lb, she merits respect on recent form.

runners_data.name: Port Of Spain
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien three-year-old whose form string reads disappointingly at 37-507, yet the good-ground placed run at The Curragh is the pick of his recent efforts; a hold-up horse who needs pace to run into, and the single front-runner here gives him less to aim at than he ideally wants.
runners_data.comment: Port Of Spain has experience over today's trip and going, and our rating places him ahead of his rivals in this field, making him a genuine top threat despite being winless in his last five starts; the concern is a career-high 138 lb in the saddle.

runners_data.name: Diamond Exchange
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners this four-year-old who won over 10f on good going last time out, and her prominent style is a genuine asset in a race where she should slot in just behind Guardian Of Realm; two wins from eight on similar ground suggests she handles it, and her OR=82 hides a horse who races to her conditions.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her proven conditions to build on; however, she carries 126 lb from stall seven and her trainer is in a lean spell at just 1/29 over the past fortnight, which tempers enthusiasm somewhat.

runners_data.name: Ob La Di
runners_data.note: Ben Coen's mount is a genuine hold-up horse from the J P Murtagh yard, 38 days since his last run, who found 10f on good ground suiting him for his placed effort at Gowran; his best recent figures have come at 13f so this slightly shorter trip is a consideration, though a decent pace would help him significantly.
runners_data.comment: Placed once in recent starts but winless in her last five, Ob La Di has run over today's trip and going before and steps back up after 38 days off; the second last time out offers encouragement, though her overall profile leaves her with plenty to prove from stall six carrying 126 lb.

runners_data.name: Akecheta
runners_data.note: Kevin Thomas Coleman's six-year-old sports a tongue-pin and has struggled to convert his good-ground starts into wins, with zero wins from nine on similar going; prominent in style and likely to track Guardian Of Realm, but his consistent finishing positions in the 5-7 range suggest he is a place horse at best here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Akecheta nonetheless catches the eye on a rating of 90 — well clear of her official mark of 81 — carrying 125 lb from stall two, and she has run over today's trip and going before, back quickly after just 16 days; the risk is that her recent finishes give little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Guardian Of Realm
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's three-year-old is the lone front-runner and should slot into the lead unchallenged; 87 days off the track is notable, and his STYLE_FIT tag flags that his OR=89 mark is framed around prominent rather than true lead duties, so setting a sustained gallop over 10.5f after a break is a non-trivial ask.
runners_data.comment: Rated well below her official mark on our figures and ranked near the foot of the field, Guardian Of Realm is hard to fancy at a 87-day absence, though her win in her last five starts and experience over today's trip and going offer slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Mocking
runners_data.note: J P Murtagh's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by nature — his single win came when the race set up late and he tracked back; shuffled into a midfield map position here because the rear is saturated, which compromises his natural game, and his soft-ground wins further temper expectations on good turf.
runners_data.comment: Mocking won four starts back but has since finished sixth twice and fourth last time out, so consistency is the question mark; he has run over today's trip and going, and 62 days off means fitness is unproven, though our rating of 86, fifth of ten, offers some encouragement from stall nine off 124 lb.

runners_data.name: Minella Rockett
runners_data.note: Reese Holohan claims 7lb on John Nallen's unexposed three-year-old who has won over both 8f and 16f on good ground, showing admirable versatility; prominent in style and likely to be competitive in second or third, making him an interesting each-way profile if he handles this class step on handicap debut.
runners_data.comment: Minella Rockett won last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, making him a clear danger from stall three on 121 lb; the worry is whether that recent winning form can be replicated stepping into stronger company.

runners_data.name: Quatre Bras
runners_data.note: A five-year-old with zero wins or placed efforts from three good-going starts, and at OR=77 the lowest-rated in the field among the competitive runners; his true hold-up style is squeezed into a midfield slot on this map, and with no realistic pace to chase him home, this shape does not suit his game at all.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a string of mid-pack finishes and a speed rating of 73 that leaves him well below the principals on our figures, Quatre Bras is hard to fancy; though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick turnaround of just eight days.

runners_data.name: Speckled Meadow
runners_data.note: Don Browne's nine-year-old is the eldest in the field and carries a 24-day turnaround into this; his natural style involves sitting last and waiting, but with the rear overcrowded his run will be further compromised — one win from 15 good-going starts tells its own story and he is likely to find this field too competitive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with placings no better than fifth, Speckled Meadow faces a stiff task ranked last on our figures, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a fresh 24-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Guardian Of Realm is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to press him, should be able to control tempo from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop over this 1m2½f trip on good ground at Naas. Diamond Exchange and Akecheta are the prominent types most likely to track him in the early positions, meaning the race will be run at a rhythm that suits those sitting just off the pace rather than generating a searching test. The field is genuinely hold-up heavy — Mocking, Quatre Bras, and Speckled Meadow are true off-the-pace horses who have been redistributed into midfield on the map simply because the rear is overcrowded, meaning their natural late runs will be compromised by the moderate pace and the traffic situation that will develop. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with tactical speed and a high cruising rate who can bridge the gap to a lone leader without needing a true sprint finish — specifically those with the class and consistency to travel smoothly in midfield and attack from 2f out on a flat track with no false pressure earlier.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Guardian Of Realm dictates a controlled tempo and the prominent/midfield pack cannot close the gap in time on flat good ground.
scenarios.body: Guardian Of Realm, uncontested at the front, sets a rhythm that suits his stamina profile and is never put under pressure until the straight, where the prominent types closest to him are ideally placed to pounce; Diamond Exchange and Minella Rockett, tracking close to the pace, are positioned to capitalise if the pace steadies and the race turns into a test of class and tactical speed from 2f out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Class Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough to string the field out and the truest hold-up types find clear ground to deliver a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Alice Monet, the highest-rated hold-up performer with strong good-ground form and a proven winning profile at this trip range, is best placed among the genuine closers to deliver a finishing run if daylight comes; Port Of Spain has the class for a similar late surge but has questions about consistency at this level.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Exchange and Akecheta both press Guardian Of Realm hard and the pace lifts enough to reward those travelling powerfully in second and third.
scenarios.body: A quicker than expected early tempo forces Guardian Of Realm to use his energy sooner, leaving Diamond Exchange and Minella Rockett — who have both won on this surface and going — to fight out the finish; this shape rewards horses who can sustain their effort from the front half of the field rather than those relying on a late sprint.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow that the entire field concertinas and the redistributed hold-up types find an uncharacteristically open late run.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability shape given that Mocking, Quatre Bras, and Speckled Meadow are all racing out of their natural role here and are unlikely to be in the tactical position needed to exploit a stop-start finish; Ob La Di, with decent good-ground placed form, is the most credible beneficiary, but even he lacks the finishing punch to overcome the positional disadvantage.

watchPoints.text: Guardian Of Realm sets fractions from the front unchallenged — watch whether he quickens or dawdles through the early stages, as a falsely slow pace will cause the entire hold-up group to bunch and scramble for ground in the straight.

Minella Rockett is ridden by a 7lb claimer (Holohan) on what looks a competitive handicap debut for the yard — watch for whether he is given a confident prominent pitch or finds himself caught in traffic if the prominent group tightens up in the first half-mile.

The three redistributed horses — Mocking, Quatre Bras, and Speckled Meadow — are all genuine hold-up types forced into midfield; watch the opening furlong to see whether any attempt to drop away to their natural position, which could cause interference or create positional chaos behind the pace.

Diamond Exchange is trained by Mrs John Harrington whose yard is running at a modest 1/29 in the last 14 days — watch the market for any confidence drift or support that might indicate stable confidence ahead of this step back up in company after winning a maiden.|

Alice Monet is ridden by 5lb claimer Sam Coen for D K Weld, a powerful combination when the yard is in form — watch whether she gets a clear run from her hold-up position, as traffic will be dense with multiple natural closers competing for the same late ground.
